correctness.rationale: First choose a nonempty edge-vertex subset in every column, with both rows represented, and allow all original vertices. This baseline has enumerator ((2z+z²)^n−2z^n)(1+z)^(n+2). It dominates all original and all unselected edge-vertices. A failure occurs only if a selected edge-vertex has no selected partner in its row or column; then it is an unpaired singleton row, and its original hub and original column endpoint must both be missing for the baseline choice to fail. For n≥3 at most one row can be singleton under column coverage. There are 2n unpaired singleton profiles, each of weight z^n, with n other free original vertices, so subtract 2nz^n(1+z)^n. This proves the entire polynomial. At degree n, the configurations use no originals and one edge-vertex per column; each row must have at least two. The constant in the bracket is 2^n−2n−2, positive from n=4. At n=3 it is zero, and the linear term is 24. Bernoulli substitution at q=1−p gives (1−q²)^n less 2(pq)^n(1+nq²), with a continuous extension at q=0. The correction is uniformly bounded by 2(n+1)4^(−n); the main term gives all three claimed limits, including the endpoints. A new exhaustive program built the middle graph by original endpoint intersections and tested domination by the union of selected open neighborhoods. All coefficients, including zeros, agreed for n=3–6 over 1,198,080 subsets. The positive totals reproduced 752, 4928, 30528 and 185344.
residual_risks: The enumeration is bounded; the proof, not extrapolation, covers all n≥3. No result claimed here for n=1,2.
